newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian metals - Dealers seek higher duty on semis.
newsitem.headline: Indian metals - Dealers seek higher duty on semis.

text.p: India's non-ferrous metals industry and trade are hopeful the government will raise import duty on semi-finished products to help protect domestic units supplying raw materials, dealers said on Wednesday.
Dealers said industrial users of non-ferrous metals were either importing or buying semi-finished products instead of raw materials because of a uniform duty on both.
At present, import duty on raw material and semi-finished items is the same at 51.80 percent, including excise and taxes.
"We have asked for a differential of 15 percent in import duty on semi-finished products and raw materials," said Bombay Metals Exchange (BME) president Sharad Parikh.
"We are hopeful the budget for 1997/98 (April/March) will keep a differential of at least 10 percent in import duty on raw materials and semi-finished products," he said.
The budget will be unveiled on February 28 in parliament.
Parikh said the market had been subdued for quite some time now, with business volumes falling steeply ahead of the budget.
Dealers said raw material purchases from local units had come down sharply as its cost was on par with imported raw material or semi-finished material.
"Users naturally prefer imported semi-finished products to local raw materials," Parikh said.
In the week to Wednesday, copper lost 150 rupees to 12,900 rupees per quintal (100 kg) while zinc gained 200 rupees per quintal to 7,100.
Tin and nickel shed 300 rupees and 100 rupees to 34,100 rupees and 37,100 rupees per quintal respectively.
Aluminium and lead were steady in dull trade.
